item.description:
Snappy 1.1

Window placement for macOS

You must re-grant Accessibility after this update

Snappy's application identity changed in this release. macOS ties the Accessibility permission to that identity and to the app's code signature, and provides no way to carry a grant from the old identity to the new one — so the permission you granted before does not apply to this build.

Until you re-grant it, Snappy will start normally and then do nothing. The leader key opens no grid and no window moves. There is no error, because as far as Snappy can tell it simply has not been allowed to move windows yet.

To fix it, after updating:

  • Open System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Accessibility.
  • If an older Snappy entry is listed, select it and remove it with −. A stale entry will not grant the new build anything.
  • Add the new Snappy with + if it is not listed, then make sure its switch is on.
  • Quit Snappy and open it again.

Your settings are not affected. Placements, layouts, snap areas and keyboard shortcuts are carried across automatically the first time this version runs. Accessibility is the one thing that cannot be.

New

  • Automatic updates. Snappy now checks getsnappy.fyi for new versions and can install them itself. Every update is EdDSA-signed and the signature is verified before anything is applied. This is the last release you have to download by hand.
  • Place a window by dragging on the grid. Bring up the placement grid, drag across the cells you want and release — the window lands exactly where you drew, whether or not that region was ever saved. Turn it off under Settings ▸ Placements ▸ Drag to place if you would rather the grid never consume a click.

Changed

  • Snappy is now published by Simarhol Onipaa LLC, which is what changed the application identity and made the Accessibility re-grant above necessary.
  • Contact for support is help@getsnappy.fyi, matching the website.
  • Snappy now requires macOS 12. Earlier releases ran on 10.15. If you are on macOS 10.15 or 11, Snappy 1.0 keeps working and this update will not be offered to you — the updater checks the requirement before proposing anything, so there is no way to install a build that cannot run.
